title: vosso actions script
description: Declarative browser flow executed by `vos record` — the recipe an agent writes after exploring a site. The recorder synthesizes the cursor track from these steps.

setup.description: Run BEFORE the camera rolls, after the first navigation: a sign-in form, a cookie banner, an onboarding tour. Plain actions with no cursor, no frames, no pace and nothing in meta.steps; then the recorder opens `url` again and the take begins where the setup left it. A selector that never appears fails the take before anything is recorded (exit 2). A `type` step's text may be { "env": "NAME" }, read at run time and never logged or stored; a literal typed into a password field is refused, because actions.json is committed and pushed.

teardown.description: Run AFTER the take, off camera, with the same verbs and rules as setup: what the take created in the product (an API key, a project, an invite) removed again, so a rehearsal or a re-record leaves the account as it found it. The steps run once the screencast has stopped, on the take's own page and session, after a --dry-run rehearsal too, and also when the take stops early or throws after its first step ran. Nothing of them is captured or written to meta.steps. Bounded at 60 s in all. A step that fails stops the teardown and is reported (the --json done event's `teardown`), and never fails the take or changes its exit code. A { "env": "NAME" } the shell does not hold refuses the take before it begins.

ready.description: When the first page counts as ready for step 1. dom: after load, once the page has made no DOM change for 800 ms, at most 8 s. networkidle: once the network has gone quiet, at most 45 s, which a page holding a socket open or an analytics beacon never does. The same mode opens a setup goto, the page after a setup, and an await's reload. `--ready` overrides. The done event's `ready` says how the first load settled ({ mode, ms, capped }); `navTimeout` is true only when networkidle was asked for and never came.

mask.description: Hidden BEFORE the first frame is captured and kept hidden across navigations and re-renders: what a signed-in account shows that must not ship. The real value is never in a frame, never in the recording, never pushed. `vos record` reports what it still sees afterwards (meta.exposures), and a mask whose selector reached nothing fails --strict.

as.description: blur the element, or swap its words for `text`. A form control is always blurred: writing into an input would change what the app submits. `text` is for IDENTIFIERS (an email, a name, an account id), never for product copy or numbers.

settle.description: every gesture step waits on the app after it (a step's own settle overrides): a canvas that falls behind under load finishes the last stroke before the next one starts

oneOf.description: Typing is a zoom signal — a type step earns a held frame on its field (the click into it opens the span, the camera releases after the last character). ~0.6s+ of typing qualifies, so pace delayMs like a person (60-90ms) for a camera moment.

ms.description: the settle after the last character, ms (default 150)

focus.description: The recorder clicks the field before typing, and that click is what opens the typing zoom on it. false types into the field as it is already focused: for a keystroke that finishes earlier typing (a submitting Enter) rather than starting it, where a second click rings a click effect on empty space beside the text.

oneOf.description: A key, a chord or a sequence, each recorded as a typing ping where the pointer is (or on selector when given, with no click), never as the key itself. key names one control key (Escape closes what a click opened, Enter submits what was typed); keys names a chord ("Shift+D", "Mod+Z", Mod being Meta on macOS and Control elsewhere), a plain key ("r", a tool's shortcut) or a sequence (["v", "Escape"]), 150 ms apart. Words are typed with type.

oneOf.description: Press-move-release: drag an element, slide a range input, move a clip. Start = selector center when given, else (x, y); end = (tx, ty), eased over ms. With path, the drag DRAWS: the press at the path's first point, a move at every later point in order (never dropped, so a page that answers slowly makes the stroke late, reported as meta.steps[].overrunMs, never a different stroke), the release at its last. modifiers are held from the press to the release.
a JSON file beside the actions file (a plain name) holding the points, or { "points": [...] }

path.description: viewport points to draw through, replayed by their own times (tMs from the first point) or, untimed, evenly over ms. A point that carries pressure draws the whole path with a pen (pointer events with that pressure); without, the mouse draws it. A path takes no selector, x, y, tx or ty

modifiers.description: held from the press to the release (Alt-drag to duplicate, Shift to constrain); Mod is Meta on macOS, Control elsewhere

ms.description: the travel of a straight drag, or of an untimed path (default 700)

oneOf.description: Check the page is as the flow expects, on camera, with no cursor move: exactly one of selector (visible; with enabled, enabled or disabled), text (some visible text contains it), gone (no longer visible) or js (an expression evaluated in the page: holds when its value is truthy, or with equals when it equals that value; for state an app keeps in script, such as a canvas's shapes). A condition that never holds is a skip with its reason (a js check names the value it last got), which --strict turns into exit 2. A js check's last value is kept on meta.steps[].value. A hosted take refuses js.

enabled.description: with selector: wait for the element to be enabled (true) or disabled (false)

js.description: a JavaScript expression evaluated in the page (a promise is awaited): the check holds when its value is truthy, or, with equals, when its value equals that one

equals.description: with js: the value the expression must answer, compared as JSON

timeout.description: seconds to wait for the condition

oneOf.description: Wait OFF CAMERA for something slow (a render, a generated result): the capture stops, the condition is polled, and the capture resumes when it holds, so the footage has no gap and no frozen stretch. The cut lands in meta.skips[] ({ step, id, at, ms }) and becomes a segment boundary in the planned doc.json. A rehearsal waits for real and prints the time.

js.description: a JavaScript expression evaluated in the page (a promise is awaited): holds when its value is truthy, or, with equals, when its value equals that one. A hosted take refuses it.

equals.description: with js: the value the expression must answer, compared as JSON

onTimeout.description: fail: the take stops there, exit 1; continue: the capture resumes and the skip records timedOut

Listed in meta.outputs[] ({ step, id, name, bytes, contentType }). A download that never arrives is a skip with its reason. A hosted take refuses a download.

src.description: a selector (the same grammar as every other step) of a video, audio or img element

as.description: the file name inside outputs/ (a plain name: no path separator, no ".."); absent, the name the page suggested

oneOf.description: Put words or a file on the clipboard and paste it the way a person's ⌘V does: the browser's own clipboard and a trusted paste chord, so the page gets a trusted keydown and paste event and navigator.clipboard.read() sees the item; when the browser refuses the item, a paste event dispatched in the page (untrusted, said in the log). Into selector (clicked first) or where the focus is. Recorded as a typing ping, never its contents. A hosted take refuses a paste.

selector.description: the element to paste into, clicked first

file.description: a file beside the actions file, by a plain name, at most 10 MB: an image (a picture other than PNG is pasted as PNG), an SVG (also as its markup), or text

ms.description: the read after the paste, ms (default 150), held from the page's last visual change like a click's

read.description: a selector whose words the recorder keeps once the step has settled (meta.steps[].text, trimmed, at most 2 KB): the take's own payload, which a layer quotes instead of a replay; on a click, what the click opened

peers.description: Other people on the page, OFF CAMERA: each a browser context of its own (its own storage state, so its own user, or signed out) on the same url, driven by its own steps. Only the take's page is filmed and only the take's steps make the cursor track; what a peer does reaches the footage through the app's own sync (its presence, its remote cursors, the shape it drew). A peer step starts with a take step (`with`, as it starts) or after one (`after`, as it ends), named by id, else right after the peer's previous step (the first, as the camera rolls). The take never waits on a peer: wait for what the peer's work shows with the take's own expect or await. A hosted take refuses peers.

id.description: a short word lines and meta.peers name the peer by

url.description: the page the peer opens (http or https); absent, the take's url

storageState.description: a Playwright storage state file (the second person's sign-in), by a path from the actions file's directory or an absolute one. Opened by the browser only: never copied into the take, never uploaded; a pushed script keeps its file name only. Absent, the peer is signed out. A peer that lands on a sign-in refuses the take.

steps.description: The peer's steps: the take's own step shapes (see steps), for wait, move, hover, click, type, press, scroll, drag (path inline only) and expect, without guard, read, caption or settle, plus when each starts. Every step is bounded like a take step; a miss is a skip listed with the take's (peer set), which --strict fails on.

with.description: start as the take's step with this id starts: the two run together

after.description: start once the take's step with this id has ended

oneOf.description: [x, y], [x, y, tMs] or [x, y, tMs, pressure]: every point timed or none

env.description: the environment variable holding the value

key.description: press: a Playwright key name (Enter, Tab, Escape)

url.description: goto: a page to open, for a sign-in that lives elsewhere

ms.description: wait: the pause; click: the read after the page settled, held from its last visual change (default 150); type and scroll: the settle after (defaults 150/200)

offCameraStep.description: One setup or teardown step: a plain action, with no cursor and no frames.
